source: design decision -- healthy baseline (no misfires) for the misfire fault hook (STEP 5, crank-resolved sidecar)
notes: 0.0=healthy convention (a probability/rate, not a _health fraction -- see health-parameter-registry.md). Implemented INSIDE each cylinder's MATLAB Function, latched once per crank cycle at the cycle-start event via a Bernoulli trial (rand() < misfire_rate): a misfired cycle has its heat release zeroed entirely, but is NOT a zero-torque cycle -- the compressed-but-unignited charge still produces a real (much smaller) blow-down torque pulse during what would be the power stroke, which is physically correct, not a bug. Verified: misfire_rate=0.5 on cylinder 1 produced real misfire events (~2 of ~5 cycles in a short window) with peak torque during a misfired cycle dropping from ~1580Nm (normal firing) to ~526Nm (compression-only blow-down) -- a genuine, correctly-directioned reduction. Duplicated per-cylinder as misfire_rate_c2/c3/c4_init, same convention.

source: design decision -- healthy baseline (no cycle-to-cycle variance) for the combustion_instability fault hook (STEP 5, crank-resolved sidecar)
notes: 0.0=healthy convention. Implemented INSIDE each cylinder's MATLAB Function, latched once per cycle at the cycle-start event as a Gaussian heat-release-magnitude multiplier (1 + combustion_stability*0.3*randn(), floored at 0) -- shared across all 4 cylinders (per the matrix, this is an engine-wide combustion-quality fault, not per-cylinder like misfire). Verified: healthy baseline gives per-cycle peak-cylinder-pressure COV=0.5% (essentially flat, small residual from slowly-rising RPM); combustion_stability=0.8 raises it to 16.6% -- a clear, correctly-directioned instability signature, matching the matrix's 'COV of IMEP rising' discriminator (peak pressure used as the validation proxy here; the sidecar's own IMEP-COV accumulator, integrating P dV per cycle properly, is still to be built).

source: assumed -- rolling-window length for the Step 5 sidecar's IMEP coefficient-of-variation accumulator, a bias/noise-vs-responsiveness tradeoff (no published standard window size)
notes: Verified: healthy baseline COV=0.44%% over this window (stable IMEP ~20.7-21.4 bar); combustion_stability=0.8 raises it to 25.4%% -- a clear, correctly-directioned signature matching the matrix's 'COV of IMEP rising' detection_signature.

source: Step 5 sidecar's TRUE crank-resolved vibration signature (angular acceleration RMS from the actual simulated shaft speed) -- NOT a fixed value, a computed telemetry channel
notes: Supersedes the Step 4 mean-value PROXY (vibration_baseline_g/vibration_imbalance_gain_g, still valid as a placeholder pending sidecar integration) for units where the sidecar is active. Cross-validated against an independent offline uniform-angle-resampled DFT of the logged omega trace (order_2x: 4073 online vs 4091 offline, order_1x: 0.7 vs 4.8 -- both near-zero as expected) -- confirms the online synchronous-demodulation algorithm is correct, not coincidentally plausible. Healthy baseline is strongly order-2-dominated (~4073 rad/s^2, the expected once-per-180-crank-degree combustion-firing signature for a 4-cylinder engine) with near-zero order-1 (no true mechanical imbalance modeled in the sidecar -- that stays the Step 4 proxy's domain). Order-tracking is computed relative to the TRUE mechanical shaft angle (mod(theta_global,2*pi)), deliberately NOT the 4*pi-periodic combustion-cycle angle, since order convention is defined relative to shaft rotation, not the thermodynamic cycle.

source: see vibration_rms_x_sidecar -- same block, same validation
notes: Injecting misfire_rate=0.3 on cylinder 1 raised order_1x from 0.7 to 12.3 (~18x) -- physically sensible: a single cylinder misfiring breaks the engine's even once-per-180-degree firing symmetry, showing up as new once-per-cycle content riding on top of the still-dominant order-2 combustion signature.

source: REUSES coolant_heat_fraction (already established for the mean-value combustion energy balance) as the Step 5 sidecar's simplified in-cylinder wall-heat-transfer loss during combustion+expansion -- NOT an independent parameter
notes: CROSS-VALIDATION FINDING: the sidecar's single-zone model is otherwise adiabatic (no gas-to-wall heat transfer term), which over-predicts IMEP substantially if the full released heat is used (fully-adiabatic run gave IMEP=29.97 bar, implying an unrealistic 56% friction fraction vs. the mean-value core's own assumed 12%). Scaling released heat by (1-coolant_heat_fraction)=0.72 before it enters the pressure ODE gives IMEP=21.61 bar (realistic for a highly-boosted CRDI diesel) and an IMPLIED friction fraction of 11.2% -- close agreement with friction_fmep_coeff's independently-derived 12%, without ever tuning to match it. Two unrelated parts of the model landing this close together is a good consistency signal, not a coincidence engineered after the fact.

source: design decision -- healthy baseline (never activates within any realistic mission) for the sensor_stuck fault hook, same channel as the other sensor faults (cht_c3)
notes: Structurally different from bias/drift/noise: a Switch+Memory sample-and-hold stage after the Sum, gated by a Step block (not a Constant -- a Constant=1 for the whole run would just hold the Memory block's t=0 IC forever, never having passed a real reading through first). Before activation, Switch passes the live signal; at activation it freezes at whatever Memory last held and re-holds itself via the feedback loop. Verified with a throttle transient (0.6->1.0 at t=1500s, activation also at t=1500s): reported_c3 frozen at exactly 88.80 from t=1500 to t=3000 while true_c3 and sibling cht1_out both moved +105.56 -- exact match to the matrix's 'channel derivative = 0 while engine_state dynamic' discriminator. Healthy case (activation=1e6) tracks true value with max|resid|=0.0000 through the same transient.

source: design decision -- healthy baseline for the fuel_starvation fault hook (STEP 4, first Tier B fault)
notes: CONDITION-GATED fault: caps max_deliverable_fuel = fuel_delivery_health*max_rated_fuel_flow via min(commanded,cap) -- does not scale delivery at all loads like injector_health does. Verified: cruise (thr=0.6) is IDENTICAL regardless of health (56.7kW/12.11kg/h both cases, matches 'invisible at cruise'); at full throttle with health=0.6, power collapses 123.5->77.1kW, RPM drops 3879.5->3291.8, fuel pins exactly at the 16.80kg/h cap -- matches the matrix's discriminator and correlated_signals (torque, rpm) exactly. Fuel deficit ratio also scales torque (engine can't make full torque without the fuel to back it) -- feeds all the way into the actual torque-balance integrator, not just a reported number, so RPM genuinely re-equilibrates lower under starvation. NOTE: building this surfaced two compounding Simulink structural bugs, not one -- see build_plan.md's Step 4 log for the full story (vector-width mismatch on the MinMax block, then Mux output-port-order instability across edits, resolved by replacing the Mux+Fcn division with a dedicated Divide block). Re-validated post-fix: healthy full-throttle 123.4kW, degraded (health=0.6) full-throttle 77.1kW/16.80kg/h -- identical to the pre-bug numbers, confirming the fix is correct and the earlier apparent-pass was coincidental, not causally correct.
